recentItems.title: Rebecca Gayheart-Dane Details New Chapter as Family After Eric Dane Death  | E! News
recentItems.description:
Six months after Eric Dane died following a battle with ALS, his family is leaning on one another. As his estranged wife, Rebecca Gayheart-Dane, and their daughters Billie, 16, and Georgia, 14, navigate their grief over losing the beloved 'Grey’s Anatomy' actor, Gayheart told E! News’ Erin Lim Rhodes in an exclusive interview. “It’s really a season of growth for all of us. Life is hard for us right now. But we are getting through, and we are soldiering on.” Gayheart and Dane were separated at the time of his death, though they remained legally married and close co-parents to their daughters. Now, Gayheart is moving toward an exciting new chapter as she works on the musical adaptation of her 1999 dark comedy Jawbreaker. For the 55-year-old, the project is about much more than a role. “I took many years off to be a stay-at-home mom,” she explained, “so now it’s really important for me to do this musical and show my kids that this is, number one, what we do as women. We go back to work. We say yes to things that are scary. And also, we do that even when life is hard.”

recentItems.title: Tupac Shakur Murder Trial: Duane "Keffe D" Davis Found Guilty | E! News
recentItems.description:
The jury has made a decision regarding the murder of Tupac Shakur. Duane "Keffe D" Davis was found guilty after being charged with one count of murder with use of a deadly weapon and with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang in 2023, following the music icon's tragic death in a 1996 shooting at 25 years old. Shakur was riding with record producer Marion "Suge" Knight in Las Vegas when a car opened fire at a red light. The "Changes" rapper died from four gunshot wounds several days later, while Knight was grazed by a bullet but ultimately survived. (In 2018, he was sentenced to 28 years in prison for unrelated manslaughter charges.) In his 2019 memoir, 'Compton Street Legend,' Davis wrote about obtaining a gun with the intent to hunt down Shakur and said he was present in the passenger seat during the shooting, Chief Deputy District Attorney Marc DiGiacomo explained in a 2023 press conference at the time the charges were indicted. Police alleged the book, as well as Davis' recollections in press interviews, was evidence the 63-year-old was a gang leader who directed the group that carried out the fatal attack, and then incriminated himself publicly over 25 years later. recentItems.title: Lionel Richie Hospitalized in ICU After Concert | E! News
recentItems.description:
Lionel Richie is on the mend. The “Hello” singer checked himself into the hospital over the weekend after performing a concert in St. Louis Aug. 29, according to multiple outlets. Richie was admitted to the intensive care unit to have tests run, with doctors looking into possible slight dehydration, according to TMZ, citing sources with direct knowledge. During the concert’s final song “All Night Long,” the American Idol judge motioned to his crew for a seat to be moved so that he could perform while sitting down, as seen in video from the event. E! News has reached out to a rep for Richie but has not received a comment. In June, Richie cut one of his concerts short after experiencing a dizzy spell—a moment he referenced during his Aug. 29 concert. For more updates on this story, visit eonline.com. recentItems.title: Hugh Hefner’s Ex Karissa Shannon Is Pregnant, Expecting First Baby | E! News
recentItems.description:
Karissa Shannon is gearing up for motherhood. The former 'Girls Next Door' star is pregnant and expecting her first child with her boyfriend of over a year, she confirmed to TMZ. Karissa—who dated Hugh Hefner while living in the Playboy Mansion from 2008 until 2010 alongside her twin sister Kristina Shannon—shared that she's two months along and recently had her first ultrasound to "confirm everything is healthy and normal." The 36-year-old—who lives in Michigan and hopes to pivot to real estate—had previously detailed her and Kristina's joint decision to leave Hollywood after living in the Playboy Mansion and starring on the final season of E!'s 'The Girls Next Door.' “It really crumbled who we are,” she told People last April, sharing that their Christian faith was frowned upon during their time in the mansion, which ultimately led them to leave. “Our believing in Jesus became a big problem, and losing that was just really big trauma that we dealt with." After a brief stint in Las Vegas, the twins made their way to Ann Arbor, Michigan, where they were able "to find out who we are and just be selfish, try and live normally." recentItems.title: Gal Gadot Says Being a Mom Unlocked Another Part of Her as an Actress | E! News
recentItems.description:
Gal Gadot's experiences with motherhood have taken her work to a new level. While discussing her new thriller, ‘The Runner,’ the actress exclusively told E! News' Will Marfuggi how becoming a mom to her daughters Alma, Maya, Daniella and Ori has changed her perspective. “Everything changes. The priority, the depth of the emotions that I felt,” Gadot said, explaining that parenthood has also given her more to draw from as a performer. In 'The Runner,' which premieres on Prime Video Sept. 2, Gadot plays Maia, a mother forced to confront every parent’s worst fear after her son is taken. Gadot shared why she could so easily connect with Maia’s drive to protect her child, adding that she would do anything to save her own children. Gadot also looked back on her time as Wonder Woman and offered a message for the actress who may one day take up the lasso. recentItems.title: D4vd's Attorneys Withdraw From Celeste Rivas Hernandez Murder Case | E! News
recentItems.description:
The legal team for D4vd—real name David Burke—have been replaced by a public defender after they requested to withdraw from the trial regarding Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s murder. During an Aug. 31 pretrial hearing, the 21-year-old “Romantic Homicide” singer said “yes” when a judge asked if he wished to receive appointed counsel, with public defender Walid Fouad Kandee subsequently taking over as his representation. Burke has pleaded not guilty to charges including murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains in the death of Celeste Rivas Hernandez, who died in 2025 at age 14. recentItems.title: How Kelly Clarkson Signed Off Her Talk Show After 7 Years | E! News
recentItems.description:
'American Idol' winner Kelly Clarkson said goodbye to 'The Kelly Clarkson Show.' Clarkson's eponymous talk show officially ended after a seven-year run on NBC and the singer proved that everyone’s life would suck without her on the air during the Aug. 31 finale. Clarkson's final episode was coined "Kelly Clarkson by Request" which allowed Clarkson's fans and audience members to request her own songs or covers for her very last Kellyokes. The "Since U Been Gone" singer also proved music will always be what defined 'The Kelly Clarkson Show,' as she dropped her new single "I'd Be Lying" along with the last episode. Naturally, Clarkson's kids River, 11, and Remington, 10—whom she welcomed with late ex Brandon Blackstock—were there in the audience. Clarkson shared a sweet supercut of all of her kids' best moments on the series and let them share their favorite memories. "I liked talking to Jason Momoa," Remington said during the broadcast, "and singing 'My Way' with the band." And River added, "I like watching you shine every single day," which got proud mama Clarkson right in the feels. recentItems.title: Rumer Willis Files Emergency Custody Request Against Ex Derek Thomas | E! News
recentItems.description:
Rumer Willis made an emergency request to a judge asking him to extend her ex Derek Richard Thomas' supervised visits with their daughter Louetta, 3, accusing him of violating their custody agreement. The filing, obtained by E! News, asks the court to bar Thomas from overnight visits with Louetta until a hearing is held—pausing a transition to unsupervised time a judge approved back in June. Willis alleged Thomas has repeatedly violated their custody terms and shown poor judgment with their daughter. Per the docs, he's completed only five and a half of his court-ordered supervised visits since they began June 20, which Willis attributes to issues with the nanny that was originally assigned to supervise Thomas' visits with Louetta. She said the nanny had to stop working due to health issues and that Thomas has refused to accept a replacement nanny. Willis also claimed that Thomas' “unsafe decisions” were demonstrated by an alleged incident in which he chose to walk two and a half miles in extreme heat with Louetta instead of taking a car, which allegedly involved him trying to cross a five-lane highway with a 55-mph speed limit. Willis was granted primary physical custody in June, with a judge also ordering a custody evaluation. That ruling had set Thomas' visits to shift to unmonitored overnights this month—the timeline Willis now wants delayed. Thomas' attorney previously called the June ruling a meaningful chance to rebuild his relationship with his daughter.
